reason: E2 directly supports the feasibility of laser-cladding TiAl-based coatings on TC4 for wear improvement via solid solution strengthening, but the specific intermetallic phases (Fe2Ti, Co2Ti) and claims about retaining substrate properties are unsupported by the cited evidence. E1 and E3 are about different materials (steel, bulk HEAs) and do not address the key premises.
premises: Laser cladding can produce TiAl-based coatings on TC4 that improve wear resistance via solid solution strengthening
TiAl-based coatings with Ni additions form hard intermetallic phases (e.g., Ni3Ti) that increase hardness
Rapid solidification during laser cladding refines microstructure and forms intermetallics in-situ
The coating maintains good metallurgical bonding with the TC4 substrate
The coating does not sacrifice TC4's beneficial properties like strength-to-weight ratio and corrosion resistance
